blocks.content: India is an indestructible union of destructible states.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 1 describes India, that is Bharat, as a 'Union of States' rather than a 'Federation of States'.
The expression 'Territory of India' is wider than 'Union of India' as it includes States, Union Territories, and territories that may be acquired by the Government of India.
Parliament holds sovereign authority under Article 3 to form new states, alter areas, boundaries, or names of existing states.
Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 for state reorganisation are not considered amendments of the Constitution under Article 368.
Cession of Indian territory to a foreign state cannot be done by a simple law under Article 3 and requires a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368.

rows: Includes States, Union Territories, and Acquired Territories
Comprises full members sharing constitutional powers with the Centre
Includes entities directly administered by the Central Government

items: Distinguish clearly between 'Union of India' (States only) and 'Territory of India' (States, UTs, and acquired territories).
A bill contemplating changes in state boundaries or names under Article 3 can be introduced in Parliament only with the prior recommendation of the President.
Settlement of a boundary dispute with another country does not require a Constitutional Amendment under Article 368; it can be executed by executive action.
